commits.headline: fix(memory): emit the recency guidance from every assembly site
commits.body:
Codex P1 (3771223810). Moving the guidance out of the token-budgeted serializer
covered voice and formatMemoryContext but missed buildPromptFromSections in
memory-context-service.js — the main chat/Slack/Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord path.
Those surfaces received the (YYYY-MM-DD) stamps with nothing telling them to
resolve wording like "tomorrow" against them, so the original failure survived
there. The serializer comment also claimed a chat-server header emitted it,
which was not true of that path.

commits.headline: fix(memory): keep the recency guidance out of the token-budgeted serializer
commits.body:
Codex P1 (3771154382). MEMORY_RECENCY_GUIDANCE is a fixed ~300 characters and
was appended to serializeMemoriesToText's header after every totalChars/charLimit
check, so it never counted toward tokenBudget. memory-cache.js calls that
function with tokenBudget: 120 (420 chars) to build voicePromptText — an
uncached block reassembled on every voice turn — so the constant more than
doubled the requested budget on the most latency-sensitive path in the system.

commits.headline: fix(memory): stamp rewritten memories with their rewrite date
commits.body:
Codex P1 (3770869167). update_memory rewrites a memory's content in place while
keeping its original creation date, but getMemoryTimestampMs only ever read the
creation fields. A memory rewritten today was therefore stamped weeks ago, and
MEMORY_RECENCY_GUIDANCE then instructed the model to resolve the NEW content's
"tomorrow" against the OLD day — reproducing the exact temporal-grounding
failure these stamps exist to prevent.

commits.headline: fix(memory): stamp recalled memories with the date they were written
commits.body:
A recalled memory is a record of something that was true when it was written,
but every live renderer emitted content only. With no age signal, absolute dates
inside a memory read as current: on 2026-08-11 a voice turn recalled a trip
itinerary stored before departure and narrated it as "drive up to Hamilton today
(Aug 1)" — after the trip had already ended. The current date WAS in that system
prompt; what was missing was how old the memory was.

commits.headline: fix(cli): re-rank corrected candidates, enforce the candidate cap per node
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. The aria-hidden correction pass now ranks the
corrected set from scratch instead of taking the first positive corrected score,
so a candidate that becomes an exact match after correction is not beaten by an
earlier prefix match. The 4000-node candidate cap is checked per node and before
each shadow-root descent rather than only on entry, and dedupe uses a Set, so a
single large root can no longer push an unbounded set through the per-node
layout and hit-test work.

commits.headline: fix(cli): walk the full ranked set, and never re-send a delivered release
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. pickClickCandidate returns `ranked` (the full ordered
set) so the aria-hidden correction pass is not capped at the three-item
runnersUp slice, which made a genuine candidate unreachable behind decoys
matching only on hidden text. The pointer sequence records which events it
delivered, so interruption cleanup cannot send a second mouseup and run
document-level release handlers twice.

commits.headline: fix(cli): confine the label-read mutation, cancel interrupted pointers, recheck disabled
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. Scoring uses plain innerText and writes nothing; only
the ranked winner is re-read with aria-hidden descendants hidden, falling through
to the next candidate if that correction kills the match. An interrupted pointer
sequence now dispatches pointercancel and mouseup on a still-connected target so
document-level pressed/drag state is not left stuck. Disabledness is rechecked
before the click event, since a mousedown handler can disable the control
mid-sequence.

commits.headline: fix(cli): exclude aria-hidden by hiding and re-reading; stop a click mid-sequence
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. aria-hidden content is excluded by setting
display:none on the outermost aria-hidden descendants, reading innerText, and
restoring the previous inline value — string subtraction could not tell which
occurrence of repeated text came from the hidden node, and was wrong in both DOM
orderings. The pointer sequence now checks isConnected between events and stops
if a handler removed the control, reporting which event it stopped before rather
than dispatching the rest at a d

commits.headline: fix(cli): score before visibility, keep disabled exact matches, use :disabled
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. The comparator now orders exact > prefix > substring
before visibility, so a visible partial match cannot outrank a hidden exact one
and dispatch a broader action. Disabled candidates are scored with the rest of
the pool and checked on the winner, so a disabled exact match is reported as
disabled rather than replaced by an enabled prefix match. Disabledness uses
matches(':disabled') plus aria-disabled instead of a fieldset[disabled] ancestor
scan, which was refusing li

commits.headline: fix(cli): disabled controls, occluded ranking, repeated aria-hidden text
commits.body:
Syncs cli-js with autohub. Disabled controls (disabled property, aria-disabled,
disabled ancestor fieldset) are excluded from candidates and rejected on the
selector path — dispatchEvent does not honour native disabled suppression, so
automation could otherwise fire a disabled destructive action. Visibility now
hit-tests at the candidate box centre so an overlay-covered control cannot win
visible-first ranking over its live duplicate. The aria-hidden subtraction
removes one occurrence per outerm

commits.headline: fix(starfield): stop the black hole repelling the stars it passes
commits.body:
Round 9's most important finding, and the only one of the batch that affects the
normal permission-granted path. The pull clearance was not capped at a star's own
home distance, so when the black hole drifted within _MinPullDistance of a home
the floor exceeded the true home-to-singularity distance and placed the star
FARTHER out than it started -- even at travel == 0, mid-dwell. A passing black
hole shoved stars away instead of drawing them in.

mask reused that same home distance instead of the star's actual rendered
position. With the shipped nonzero pull

quantity while a second quantity that also determines the outcome escapes it.
The round-2 fix capped the ring's RADIUS below the wearer's head distance, but

"distant" treatment distance of 1.6m, that 1.8m width alone exceeded the
entire available clearance, so a radius floored to

commits.headline: fix(starfield): fall back to the volume's farthest corner, not just its longest axis
commits.body:
7ea37ef5 fixed which axis the exhausted-rejection-sampling fallback used, but never
checked that point against InnerRadius. For settings where valid space exists only
near the volume's corners (e.g. a 2x2x2 volume with InnerRadius 1.6), all 16
uniform attempts routinely miss that thin region, and the longest-axis fallback,
(1, 0, 0), sits at magnitude 1 -- inside the 1.6m exclusion sphere the generator
exists to enforce, placing a star inside the black hole.

commits.headline: fix(starfield): cap the shockwave ring below the wearer's actual head distance

from the wearer -- so at shipped defaults (RoomRingRadius 2m) a black hole sitting
between the 1.5m "distant" treatment threshold and that 2m ceiling let the shell
expand straight through the viewer's head before the dial's own cap ever engaged.
Same defect shape as _MinPullDistance (fixed in 02a58126): a floor bounded an
input, not the actual outcome. The Vert now measures the live distance from the
singularity to

commits.headline: fix(starfield): make the field's radial scale answer the live beat, not a static offset
commits.body:
_FieldExpansion and _InflowRate are amplitude dials that BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels
republishes as tuning constants every frame, so folding them straight into
radialScale produced a fixed offset rather than a breath -- the Field | Inflow role
existed specifically to make the room expand and contract with the pulse, and it
never did. _BeatEnergy is the one channel that actually varies with the beat, so it
now gates how much of the dialed range applies each frame, the same
envelope-times-amplitude

commits.headline: fix(starfield): size mesh bounds to the dials' actual permitted expansion
commits.body:
TrialGStarfieldMesh.Create padded bounds by a flat 25% over the baked
volume, but TrialGStarfield.shader's Vert can scale a star's radial
distance by up to 2x (radialScale = 1 + _FieldExpansion - _InflowRate,
each clamped to [0, 1] by BlackHoleVisualTuning). fieldExpansion ships at
1.0 today, so a low inflowRate during a tuning sweep could pop stars out
of the frustum edge -- Unity culls against these baked bounds, not the
vertex shader's runtime result.

commits.headline: fix(starfield): pick the volume's actual longest axis for the sampling fallback
commits.body:
TrialGStarfieldMesh.SampleHome's exhausted-rejection-sampling fallback
always placed its point on Z at the volume's longest half-extent, even
when X or Y was the longer axis. An 8x4x2 volume's longest axis is X, so
the fallback returned (0, 0, 4) -- 4m out on a Z axis whose half-extent is
only 1m, outside both the volume and the mesh bounds.

commits.headline: fix(starfield): enforce the min pull distance on a star's final position
commits.body:
_MinPullDistance only ever floored the pull-strength denominator in
TrialGStarfield.shader's Vert; the destination lerp toward the singularity
was unbounded, so a close pass could still carry a star to within ~4% of
the singularity despite the dial. The comfort guarantee it advertises --
no star ever yanked through the wearer's face -- was false as written.

commits.headline: test(starfield): pin the shockwave's -1 no-ring sentinel, not just its 0 amount
commits.body:
Shader_ExposesTheBoundedRingRadius asserted _ShockwaveAmount defaults to 0
but left _ShockwavePhase's -1 default unpinned. -1 is the load-bearing
value -- it is what keeps Vert's `if (_ShockwavePhase >= 0.0)` branch
closed on a material nobody writes to. If that sentinel ever drifted to 0
the branch would go live every frame on an unwritten material; the amount
defaulting to 0 only zeroes the magnitude, not the branch.

commits.headline: feat(starfield): send the shockwave into the room, bounded
commits.body:
The room-scale starfield now answers the Shockwave channel: the spike
withheld it deliberately, reasoning that a ring thrown across the whole
room reads as a screen effect rather than an object in the world. That
objection stands, so the ring is capped at _RoomRingRadius in the vertex
shader (fill-rate budget, not fragment) and dissolves before it reaches
the wearer, and is gated on _SingularityWS.w the same way the pull is, so
a disabled channel writer cannot fire a ring from a ghost position.

commits.headline: fix(starfield): stop a disabled channel writer from publishing a ghost singularity
commits.body:
OnDisable's PublishChannels call ran while _hasPublishedSingularity was still
true (by design, to avoid re-latching against the pre-disable position), which
meant it published w=1 with the stale last-known position. BlackHoleVisualTuning's
DefaultPullStrength (1f) and DefaultInfallRate (0.35f) are already non-zero, so
the moment a future task wires those dials to the shader, a disabled writer would
leave every star pulling toward a black hole that is no longer there.

commits.headline: feat(starfield): let the black hole eat the room
commits.body:
Adds the singularity pull to TrialGStarfield.shader's Vert: inverse-square
falloff from _SingularityWS, a hash-phased per-star home -> horizon -> home
infall cycle, and an alpha fade so a star reads as consumed rather than
teleported. _PullStrength and _InfallRate default to 0, so a material
nobody writes to keeps rendering exactly as it did before this task.

TrialGSummonCue.LateUpdate fell into an "else return" whenever

in after a second pinch, a grab/lasso takeover, a lost target pose, or

last drew, so both gold hand rings stayed stuck on screen indefinitely
after a cancelled recall. c90f671d's arrival-distance guard made this

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): gate calm growth on trustworthy signal
commits.body:
BlackHoleHeartbeatPulse.calmTarget was scaled by PulseAmplitude alone,
which ramps toward 1 on measurement freshness regardless of contact
state. A contact-capable strap that keeps streaming NotDetected after
it comes off therefore kept being treated as genuine calmness, holding
the black hole enlarged — the same failure mode e3c36945 gated
_BeatEnergy against, left open on the calm-growth path.

commits.body: Package the Modes/Parakeet/enhancement cutover checklist for public skillissue install, with backup validator and launch copy.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): verify arrival distance before raising SummonArrived
commits.body:
TrialGPhysicsController ends a recall (EndRecallDrive) purely because
its fixed-duration curve elapsed, whether or not the body actually
reached the target -- a room collider blocking the dynamic body ends
the drive the exact same way as a clean delivery. TrialGSummonController
read IsRecalling == false alone as "arrived" and raised SummonArrived
unconditionally, so a recall blocked behind a wall could still announce
arrival while the black hole stayed far outside ArrivalDistance.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): give the summon flash a signal-independent gain
commits.body:
The summon gesture works with no heart-rate source connected, but its
body flash was multiplied by `warm` (_WarmColor * _WarmAmount), and
_WarmAmount is 0 by default until a live rate produces calmness. In a
release session where BLE has not connected -- the default state for
any wearer without a strap -- the hand rings would announce a summon
arrival while the black hole itself answered with nothing.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): reject non-finite values in the UDP tuning protocol
commits.body:
float.TryParse accepts "NaN" and "Infinity" as well-formed numbers, and
neither Mathf.Clamp nor Mathf.Clamp01 sanitizes them -- both of Clamp's
comparisons are false for NaN, so it passes straight through. A message
like "beatsizeamount=NaN" over UDP could therefore reach
BlackHoleVisualTuning.BeatSizeAmount, which now feeds directly into
pulseTarget.localScale (BlackHoleHeartbeatPulse.LateUpdate), poisoning
the black hole's transform.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): gate published beat energy on trustworthy signal
commits.body:
BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels published _BeatEnergy unconditionally even
when BlackHoleBeatTreatmentMath.HasTrustworthySignal was false (e.g. a
contact-capable strap reporting NotDetected). PulseAmplitude ramps up
from measurement freshness alone, so the envelope stayed nonzero and
TrialAEmissive/TrialAParticles kept brightening and expanding the body
after the strap was removed, contradicting the "strap removed -> warm
response goes to nothing" acceptance criterion.

commits.headline: chore(heartbeat): serialize the new shader channels into the materials
commits.body:
Unity writes newly-declared shader properties into every material that uses
the shader. These are all default values (0, or -1 for _ShockwavePhase's
"no ring" sentinel) plus the authored _WarmColor tint, so nothing renders
differently — but committing them keeps a fresh checkout from showing five
permanently-dirty materials.

commits.headline: feat(heartbeat): settle the shockwave ring at a moderate default
commits.body:
Set from the user's own on-device verdict during the live tuning session:
the ring reads clearly at 0.7 without dominating the composition. This was
the last dial left unsettled — deliberately held back until the thin-annulus
routing bug and the warm-gate floor were both fixed, since neither the ring
nor the treatment itself was judgeable before that.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): blend treatment weights instead of cutting between them
commits.body:
The spec asks for continuous weights so crossing a treatment boundary
does not pop. TreatmentBlendHalfLife existed as a pinned constant with
nothing reading it — BlackHoleHeartbeatChannels assigned
ResolveWeights' output to _weights directly, so crossing the 1.5 m
distance band was a one-frame cut from (size 1.0, ember 0.7) to
(shockwave 1.0). The half-life's own contract test asserted only the
constant's value, which would pass against this no-op.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): surface emberAmount and shockwaveAmount on the tuning HUD
commits.body:
The tuning page showed MIX/BAND/FORCED/FIELD/INFLOW/WARM/BEAT/LAST but
omitted emberAmount and shockwaveAmount — the one dial the plan
explicitly leaves unsettled pending the user's on-device re-judgement.
During that session the wearer would turn the shockwave dial and get no
on-screen confirmation it landed, only the LAST line's raw echo of the
last accepted message, which is one message stale.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): wire BeatSizeAmount into the pulse's size treatment
commits.body:
BeatSizeAmount was advertised by tune-udp.py, parsed and clamped by
BlackHoleVisualTuning.TryApply, reset by ResetToDefaults, pinned by a
test and displayed live on the tuning HUD as "BEAT: 0.06" — but nothing
consumed it. A dial that reports success and does nothing is worse than
an absent one: a developer sends beatSizeAmount=0.3, watches the HUD
confirm it, and sees no change.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): give the warm gate a floor the tuning rig can reach
commits.body:
_WarmAmount gated every warm treatment (ember, shockwave ring, breath
bloom, summon flash) as calmness * WarmAmount. Calmness is exactly 0 at
90+ BPM and ~0.39 at a normal standing 75 BPM, so at an elevated heart
rate treatment selection had no visible effect at all — and because
WarmAmount was a multiplier, sending warmAmount=1 over UDP could not
force it back on. The tuning rig structurally could not reach the
failure it exists to let a developer diagnose.

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): clear the tuning HUD page before redrawing it
commits.body:
RedrawTuningPage() drew directly onto the persisted pixel buffer without
clearing it first, unlike Redraw()'s page-0 path. DrawText/DrawGlyph only
set lit pixels, never clear the surrounding cell, so BAND, FORCED, and
LAST — the fields most likely to shrink between redraws while parked on
page 1 during live tuning — could leave stale glyph fragments from the
previous, longer text bleeding through. Mirrors the same full-buffer
FillRect(BackgroundColor) that Redraw() already does before drawing.

SetPage) and a `page=N` command to BlackHoleVisualTuning.TryApply, driven
by BlackHoleVisualTuning.RequestedHudPage over the UDP tuning channel.
Page 1 shows active treatment mix, distance band, forced treatment, the
field/inflow/warm/beat dials, and the last tuning message.

preconditions fail silently: a null line array or an unresolved target

commits.headline: feat(trial-g): zip the summon back on an eased sub-second curve
commits.body:
The recall drove through the lasso's Selected path, which is deliberately
gentle — 0.55 m/s, eased in over 0.3 s — because it is a manipulation. A
room crossing at that speed took about five seconds, which is why the
timeout was six. A recall is a restart, not a manipulation, so it gets its
own drive: a fixed 0.6 s flight regardless of distance, so the gesture
reads the same whether the hole is across the room or just out of reach.

rather than as twitching on ordinary respiratory variation. It multiplies
with the beat envelope, so a slow heart is a large black hole that is still
visibly beating. Neither multiplier touches the black hole's diameter, which
also sizes the SphereCollider used to grab it.

and wipe it. A degraded hub returning `200 {"tasks": []}` while its task
store is unavailable decodes to an authoritative-looking empty array, so
pruning on it caused the exact data loss this branch guards against.

commits.body:

stale-payload branch (the early return taken when the remote `updatedAt` is
not newer than the local one). That branch is exactly how a terminal status
arriving on an older-stamped payload clears a stranded `needs_input`
attention, so tasks could stay parked in "needs you" forever after they
finished.

calibration.js buckets on decisionClass alone, so a window spanning a model
change averages two different judges into one number -- and judge-promotion.js
could promote a class to live on that mixed sample. This adds the column that
makes a pre/post comparison possible at all, and must land before the judge's
model changes.
